source: Dr. Thaveesak Sangudom, Dr. Theerawut Chutinanthakun, and Wirot Horasart, "Off-season Production Techniques for Pursat Orange (ក្រូចពោធិ៍សាត់ / kroch poursat) in Cambodia," in The Guideline of Climate Change Adaptation in Cambodia (pp. 130-153), Project on Promoting Climate Resilience in Farming Communities of Cambodia, General Department of Agriculture (GDA) Cambodia, Thailand International Cooperation Agency (TICA), and Department of Agriculture (DOA) Thailand, 2017-2020.
text:
The source provides a month-by-month production calendar for off-season Pursat orange, built around a harvest in August-September:

- September: harvest.
- October: prepare trees for the next season (late in the month).
- November: prune (cut dead branches and any branch growing into the tree's center); apply the post-harvest fertilizer round (organic fertilizer 5-10 kg/tree plus NPK 15-15-15 at 0.5-2 kg/tree, amount depending on trunk diameter); irrigate; and begin pest/mite monitoring and spraying as needed.
- December: irrigate adequately throughout the month; continue pest monitoring and spraying as needed; new leaf flush begins and flowering starts late in the month.
- January: continued bud/fruit development; irrigate throughout; continue pest monitoring and spraying as needed.
- February: NPK 15-15-15 at 0.3-0.5 kg/tree (1-2 months after fruit set); irrigate throughout; continue pest monitoring and spraying as needed.
- March: irrigate throughout; continue pest monitoring and spraying as needed.
- April: NPK 15-15-15 at 0.3-0.5 kg/tree (3-4 months after fruit set); irrigate throughout; continue pest monitoring and spraying as needed.
- May: irrigate to manage soil moisture early in the month; pest monitoring/spraying as needed early in the month.
- June: NPK 13-13-21 at 0.5-1.0 kg/tree (1-2 months before harvest); irrigate throughout; pest monitoring/spraying as needed.
- July: irrigate throughout; continue pest monitoring and spraying as needed.
- August: harvest; sort, grade by size, and pack fruit.
- September: harvest continues; sort, grade, and pack; record the season's results in the final week.

This calendar consolidates the individual practices described in the other entries in this batch (pruning, fertilizer schedule, irrigation, pest/disease monitoring, harvest) into a single seasonal timeline.
caveat: The calendar in the source marks specific weeks (1-4) within each month with checkmarks for each practice. Reading exact checkmark placement reliably from a rasterized table image is harder to guarantee than reading printed text, so the month-level timing above should be treated as reliable, while week-level precision within a given month is lower-confidence and worth a second check against the original if a farmer-facing app needs week-level accuracy.
